replay-nalox: The trouble breathing on that list can't always wait for medics, because slow, shallow breathing can mean an opioid overdose, which naloxone reverses, so if you have a naloxone nasal spray, spray it into one nostril right away. It doesn't matter if they think they only took MDMA, since fentanyl, an opioid, has turned up in pills sold as MDMA, and naloxone does no harm if they took no opioid. But naloxone can wear off before the opioid does, so call medics even if they wake up, and if their breathing slows again before the medics come, give them the second spray in the pack.
